newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi harvest advances, cotton needs warmth.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi harvest advances, cotton needs warmth.

text.p: Harvesting of corn, rice, sorghum and soybeans advanced in Mississippi during the week ended Sunday, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.

Cotton needed dry weather to allow farmers to defoliate the plants. The crop was rated 18 percent excellent, 50 good, 27 fair, four poor and one very poor. Seventy-seven percent had open bolls versus 57 a year ago and the 43 average.
Corn was 38 percent harvested versus 41 a year ago and the 28 average. The crop was rated 13 percent excellent, 56 good, 25 fair, five poor and one very poor.
Rice was 18 percent harvested versus 20 a year ago and the 13 average. The crop was rated 18 percent excellent, 59 good, 22 fair and one poor.
Sorghum was 53 percent harvested versus 37 a year ago and the 26 average. The crop was rated 13 excellent, 58 good, 24 fair, four poor and one very poor.
Soybeans were nine percent harvested versus none a year ago and for the average. The crop was rated 13 percent excellent, 58 good, 24 fair, four poor and one very poor.
Soil moisture was rated 21 percent surplus, 64 adequate, 12 short and three very short.
